WORDRAMP — by Mr. Saymaz
v0.27.0 · Rides & Bridges

Wordramp is the new name of Wordrift. Saved progress, stars and arena wins
carry over unchanged.

RIDES (EVERY ROUTE CHOICE)
A billboard before each route choice promises a ride. Steer into the right
answer and its track snaps up out of the ground ahead; the car is launched
and lands gently back in its own lane.
- Sunlit Boulevard, Sky Coaster: three rides that build up through the race.
  The first is gentle (launch, drop, helix); the second adds a vertical loop
  and a corkscrew; the finale has the biggest drop, a double loop, a double
  corkscrew and a wide helix.
- Coastal Overpass, Sea Jumps: a low hop first; then a long flight over the
  sea with a barrel roll at the top; the finale is a double jump (a landing
  platform launches a second, higher flight with a double roll). Each ends
  on a landing deck and wave rollers.
- Stormcrest Expressway, Cliff Plunges: a short climb and drop first; then
  one through rock arches; then the full plunge with bobsled half-pipe
  swerves; the finale climbs 22 m, drops almost vertically, corkscrews
  inside the rock arches and swerves for longer.
The track stays hidden until your answer is judged, so it never gives the
answer away. Rides are for fun: each gains the same 18 m as an ordinary
shortcut (the real reward is not taking the slow detour) and can never cost
a hit. Rivals who answer right ride the passing track beside you. Reduced
motion keeps every ride with lower drops and no loops, rolls, helix or
swerves.

BRIDGE OUT (ROAD REPAIR)
The road ahead breaks over a gap. Connect the three sentence blocks in order:
each correct block drops its word slab into the gap with a note (a crane in
Sunlit, drawbridge leaves in Coastal, carved stone in Stormcrest), and the
full sentence plays a little chime. A wrong block's slab wobbles and swings
back out; the slabs already placed stay. Then drive over your sentence: each
word lights up under the wheels, with a small hop off the end.

PICTURE SIGNS
Some vocabulary signs show a 3D Fluent Emoji picture: choose the word that
matches the picture, or steer into the picture that shows the word.

NETLIFY DEPLOYMENT
For a build-based deployment, use the whole extracted project. The included
netlify.toml specifies Build command: npm run build; Publish directory: dist.
Leave the base directory blank (the project root). The build recreates dist
with all game files, even if dist has been deleted.
For manual drag-and-drop, upload the dist folder inside this ZIP. It already
contains index.html, game.bundle.js, styles and the language banks.
See README.md at the project root for setup and rebuilding instructions.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.24.0
- New cars for you, your rivals and traffic; three art-directed arenas with
  landmarks, coastal tunnels, rain in Stormcrest and smoother scenery.
- Phone HUD shows clock, position, Nitro and Pause in one row. Portrait
  phones see all three lanes beside the car.
- Rivals race fairly: no brake-checking in your escape lane, no stuck cars,
  and Relaxed is competitive instead of an automatic win.
- Richer engine, Nitro and arena sound; the world quietens while you read.
- Traffic arrives in small groups to weave through, busier in later arenas
  and on Challenge. Mr. Saymaz guides you on the menus and results.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.23.1
- Holding acceleration or Nitro commits to open-road driving without
  proximity braking. Release acceleration/Nitro to coast and brake safely.
  A real bumper contact causes damage; cars keep their physical separation.
- Impact recovery lasts 3 seconds. Rivals keep driving through clear lanes
  and can close the gap or pass. Their positions never jump.
- Nitro stays saved while the car is pinned after an impact. Crossings and
  English-task autopilot retain their safe stopping and shared pace rules.
- All failures now clearly show DNF / DID NOT FINISH. An earlier lead is
  never presented as first place. Failure screens have no race podium.
- Broken cars, failed races and stale finish data cannot earn Ulti points,
  race stars or arena unlocks. Every retry starts fully repaired.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.23.0
- Three condition marks below the clock show how many hits remain.
- First hit: cracked glass, dented paint, sparks and brief speed loss.
  Second hit: loose bonnet and panel, light smoke, one hit left.
  Third hit: engine sputters to a stop and the race ends in a breakdown.
- A continuing scrape counts once. Relaxed gives 3 seconds of protection;
  Challenge gives 2 seconds. Rivals catch up through normal driving while
  you recover, with no position jumps.
- Wrong English answers never damage your car. Guided English tasks and
  their protected exits remain safe. Each new race starts fully repaired.
- Reduced motion retains the damage cues without particles or impact shake.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.22.0
- Phone/tablet bottom buttons are replaced with a continuous thumb gesture.
  Hold the road to accelerate, swipe left/right to steer, slide up for Nitro,
  and slide down to keep regular acceleration while saving the Nitro charge.
- Slide farther up to add a second or third charge. Holding still never buys
  additional charges. Lift your finger to release driving and Nitro.
- A small non-interactive Nitro/fuel meter sits beside race position. During
  English tasks it becomes subdued. The lower road stays clear for fingers.
- Autopilot, finger connections, category choices and desktop controls remain.
  The phone preview uses the new touch layout even with a desktop mouse.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.21.0
- The four grade files expand the existing units through matching sub-themes.
  Lessons shows the included sub-themes under each unit description.
- Added 341 vocabulary translations, 264 definition clues, 132 short Q&A
  signs, 132 grammar choices and 438 three-block road repairs.
- Pedestrian crossings rotate category pairs for greater vocabulary variety.
- All 44 existing lesson titles, unit IDs and progress keys are preserved.
- The ZIP includes the original source files, reviewed choices, mapping report
  and repeatable importer. Ambiguous source endings stay out of driving tasks.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.20.4
- Holding the car no longer starts native text selection, image dragging or
  the browser's touch callout menu on game content. Old selection is cleared
  when starting a race or touching the road.
- Driving holds, Nitro, lane swipes and road-repair connections keep working.
  Lesson/settings scrolling and native form controls remain available.
- The Netlify project still builds and publishes the complete dist folder.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.20.3
- Source assets live in public; npm run build copies them into dist and
  bundles the application there. Missing local HTML assets fail the build.
- The release ZIP keeps the source checkout layout and includes netlify.toml
  plus a prebuilt dist. Build-based and manual deployments use the same game.
- A clean extracted-ZIP build and empty-dist regression verify deployment
  output. Gameplay and Lessons behavior are unchanged.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.20.2
- The lesson button opens Lessons / Choose your lesson, with Grade 5 A1,
  Grade 6 A1+, Grade 7 A2 and Grade 8 A2+ options.
- Every unit card has its number, a bold full title and a short description
  of the language it covers. All 44 unit descriptions follow the material.
- Grade choices and Apply/Cancel remain visible while scrolling the list.
  Very short landscape screens scroll the full pop-up. Close/Escape cancels.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.20.1
- Theme / Unit uses a numbered vertical list rather than a dropdown. Each
  unit has its own row with its complete title. Long titles wrap naturally.
- Choose a grade to show its units in curriculum order. Tap a row to select;
  Apply saves your choice. Cancel/Escape preserves your current lesson.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.20.0
- Finish first to unlock the next arena, separately for every unit and mode.
  Second/third place still keep English stars, fuel and mastery. Review laps
  and unfinished races do not unlock arenas. Existing recorded first-place
  wins still count; stars alone do not prove a victory.
- After choosing, hold your car, the speed button or Up to shorten the slow-
  motion return to about 0.25 seconds. A control already held works too.
  Release to keep the remaining gentle fade. Normal acceleration resumes
  from the same live hold, without lifting and pressing again.
- Road repairs must be correct and visitors must clear the crossing before
  the quick return can start. Lane choices wait for physical alignment and
  remain graded at the road line. Unanswered tasks keep their thinking time.
- Nitro is conserved during focus and rivals cannot gain ground during it.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.19.0
- The opening screen follows the reference layout: three illustrated arena
  tiles, four team crest cards with their English League points, a lesson card
  beside a vertical Relaxed / Challenge choice, and a wide start button.
- Tap the lesson card to choose Grade 5–8 and the matching Unit. The complete
  unit title is shown. Apply commits it; Cancel keeps your previous lesson.
  Wordrift colours, branding, car paints, stars and saved progress remain.
- More driving obstacles fill the open stretches. The safe gap holds for a
  short two-row beat, then moves to an adjacent lane. Opening rows and lane
  changes have an unambiguous gap. Full left-to-right jumps are avoided.
- Coastal Overpass adds tire stacks and loose road panels; Stormcrest adds
  rockfall debris. Later arenas have more obstacles and shorter row spacing.
  Full task approaches, construction, crossings and route merges stay clear.
- Civilian cars follow the changing road gaps with signalled, continuous
  movement, preventing a queue from blocking the available path. Guided
  shortcuts make a little room for a close rival without changing the route.
- Grade/unit controls, geometry, obstacle escalation, traffic clearance,
  racing, focus cruise and browser viewport checks pass. Actual phone
  appearance, touch feel and performance still need device playtesting.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.18.0
- Complete words fit their road signs. Font sizing measures the actual font
  and available card width, including padding and borders. Only spaces wrap;
  hyphenated words stay together. Category titles use readable title case.
- Traffic lights and route choices enter green-gold focus cruise 52 metres
  before the road line. The distant approach stays at normal driving pace.
- The dashboard holds the entry speed while the world slows. Steering, sign
  taps and keyboard lane choices remain active. A deliberate choice that
  settles in its lane begins a smooth return, without a long lock-in wait.
- Answers are still judged at the physical road line; forks begin there.
  You can correct a choice before arrival. Each task enters focus once.
- Open-road legs are 600m longer overall per arena to keep reading-paced
  races around five minutes with the quicker task exits.
- Nitro is saved during focus. Live held acceleration resumes after the
  return. Rival pacing stays protected, including through the return.
- Controlled traffic clears the answer lanes promptly during focus.
  Relaxed rivals use stronger fuel-funded boosts for a competitive finish.
- Font-fit, lane placement, focus/input, movement and full-race checks pass.
  Browser appearance and real-phone touch/performance need playtesting.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.17.0
- Pedestrian tasks now use the same green-gold slow motion and temporary
  autopilot as road repairs. They begin earlier, 150 metres before the
  crossing, while the speedometer holds the car's entry speed.
- Sort all four visitors while approaching. Normal time returns smoothly
  once the last person reaches the pavement, so timely sorting avoids a
  full stop. If people remain on the stripes, the car safely waits.
- Up, a car touch or the speed-button touch can stay held through autopilot,
  or be pressed during its return. Acceleration resumes automatically.
  Release to cancel. The speed button stays responsive and marks a hold.
- Pause, cancelled pointers and window blur clear held inputs. Pause still
  needs a new input when resumed; autopilot completion does not.
- Left/right controls sort pedestrians while autopilot holds the lane.
  Nitro is conserved through focus, crossing waits and the guided exit.
  Rival pacing remains fair, and the denser obstacle sequences remain.
- Automated movement, input, crossing-safety and race checks pass. Actual
  browser appearance and real-phone touch/performance need playtesting.

WHAT CHANGED IN v0.14.0
- Nitro is now held, released and saved. Hold NITRO or Space to use it;
  release to conserve the remaining charge. Holding the car / accelerator
  or Up arrow also resumes a charge already loaded for this race.
- A new charge costs 30 fuel. Hold again to resume a saved charge for free,
  even at zero fuel. Tap the small +30 button or press N to add another
  charge level, up to three. Resuming never buys another charge.
- An upward road swipe boosts while your finger stays down. Lift to save.
  English tasks, occupied crossings, guided exits and blocked traffic
  conserve the reservoir. Pause and cancelled touches release all holds.
- The Nitro control shows saved seconds and stays usable at maximum charge
  or with no fuel left. Charge purchase and use now have distinct controls.
  Exhaust and launch rings respond when boosting actually starts/resumes.
- Spectators watch and cheer from tiered viewing platforms behind barriers.
  Flags flutter as racers pass; optional ambience and applause fade near
  stands. Crowd audio is quiet during reading. Battery saver reduces crowd
  density; reduced motion stills cheering and flags. Pause freezes them.
- Crowd stands are pooled and reassigned only after passing out of view.
  Viewing areas avoid the English task buffers and branching roads.
- Cars have clearer team roof markings, the HUD shows the selected team,
  and the coast has offshore sailboats. Controls have steadier numeric
  readouts, clearer saved/active states and a separate charge button.

OPEN THE GAME
Extract the ZIP and open index.html in a current browser with WebGL enabled.
The playable build includes its assets and does not require a CDN.
The hosted preview remains private to its owner. To share with students,
place the playable files on your static host with index.html at its top level.
Portrait is the main mobile layout; landscape also adapts.

CHOOSE YOUR LESSON
Choose a team, Grade 5, 6, 7 or 8, a theme/unit, and Relaxed or Challenge.
All 44 units from Tower Swarm v0.14.11 remain available:
Grade 5: 10. Grade 6: 10. Grade 7: 12. Grade 8: 12.
Complete arenas in order: Sunlit Boulevard, Coastal Overpass, Stormcrest.
Each lasts about five minutes at a reading pace, with 12, 14 or 16 tasks
and roughly 570–610m between them. Acceleration and Nitro shorten a run.

CONTROLS
- Phone/tablet: hold anywhere on the road to accelerate. Keep your thumb down
  and swipe left/right to change lanes. Repeat swipes without lifting.
- Slide the same thumb forward and hold for Nitro. Slide it down to save the
  unused charge while staying accelerated. Slide farther forward for a second
  or third charge. Lifting the thumb releases both acceleration and Nitro.
  Fuel and saved Nitro appear beside race position; no bottom buttons remain.
- Desktop: use Left/Right or A/D, or the on-screen arrow buttons. Hold Up,
  the car or the speed button to accelerate. Hold Space or NITRO to boost;
  release to save charge. Press N or tap +30 to add a charge, up to three.
  Holding desktop acceleration also uses an already-loaded charge.
- Each new charge costs 30 fuel; resuming one is free. A fixed touch hold
  never purchases more charges. The desktop speed display uses up to 90 km/h
  for regular acceleration and 200 km/h for maximum Nitro.
- Tap the full-text answer sign, steer into its lane, or press 1 / 2 / 3.
  Each lane holds one answer. English tasks stay on the road.
- For road repairs, drag through the three blocks in sentence order.
  Tapping blocks or using 1 / 2 / 3 also works. Correct repairs are immediate.
- At crossings, swipe a visitor's word left/right, tap a category, or use
  the arrows. All cars wait until the pedestrians have reached the sidewalk.
- Escape / P pauses. Losing focus also pauses and releases held controls.

RACING AND ENGLISH
Correct first-try English earns 10 fuel; every third answer in a streak
adds 5 more. Fuel is saved between runs. Driving never requires spending it.
Wrong answers cost 1.5 seconds. Bumps cost 3 seconds in Relaxed and 5 in
Challenge. Correct shortcuts add 3 seconds; wrong routes are recoverable
longer detours. Three Nitro stages have stronger acceleration and effects.
Tasks, occupied crossings and correct-exit recovery protect racing ground:
rivals cannot advance farther than the player during those phases. Nitro
charges pause while waiting. Rivals use the same regular top-speed ceiling
and cannot start with more fuel than the player. Their boosts cost fuel.
Stars reward English accuracy and clean driving, separately from race place.
Missed items return with a different clue; a short review lap is also offered.

ENGLISH LEAGUE
Arena wins add Ulti points to your grade's team in Mr. Saymaz's English
League. Tap LEAGUE · GRADE n in the garage to see the four teams. The result
screen shows what your win added. Offline wins are sent later.
Teachers: config.js holds the League address. Set ultiApi to '' for a
practice-only copy with no League connection.

Which wins count: a first place with enough tasks right first time
(Relaxed: 60%; Challenge: 2+ stars, 75%). The League decides the points and
daily limits. The garage team cards show each team's League points for your
grade. A first place below that accuracy earns nothing and the result says
why. Your team is locked for the current run. Ulti points live only in the
English League; the old browser-only team points are retired. See
ULTI_INTEGRATION.md.

MASTERY AND SETTINGS
At 90% first-try accuracy, Explorer requires 6 distinct items and one arena;
Scholar requires 12 and two arenas; Master requires 18 and all three arenas.
Equip badges and the Master Aurora trail in Customise car. Team choice
controls the body colour. Settings include sound, vibration, motion comfort
and Auto/High/Battery saver rendering. Reduced motion steadies the camera
and reduces celebration/boost effects. Auto adapts rendering resolution.
Stars, fuel, mastery, team choice and points are saved in this browser.

VALIDATION
Automated checks cover team colours, mandatory team choice, star migration,
first-place-only awards, unique run IDs, duplicate prevention after reload
and expiry, independent 72-hour expiries, and unchanged timestamps on export.
Road checks compare containment with rendered fork triangles and simulate
both shoulder exits, civilian fork routing, obstacle planning, physical
spacing, continuous movement and safe pedestrian queues. English reading
protection is checked at 30/60/120 Hz. Competition and pacing simulations
cover both difficulties and all arenas. Language checks cover all 44 units.
Held-input checks cover release/resume, no repeat purchase, blocked traffic
and saved charge at 30/60/120 Hz. Crowd checks cover off-road fan transforms,
hidden-only stand recycling, proximity reactions and paused/reduced motion.
UI interaction uses a DOM double; 3D checks use a mocked renderer. These
verify logic and geometry. Real-device appearance, performance and touch
playtesting remain unverified.

SOURCE AND REBUILD
app.js: interface and interactions.
scene.js: 3D scene; road-layout.js: lane signs and strokes.
teams-ulti.js: teams and which wins are claimed from the English League.
league.js: English League connection (pools, start, claim, outbox).
spectators.js: pooled viewing stands, instanced fans and cloth.
progression.js: saved mastery, badges and compatibility migration.
driving-feel.js: steering and car movement.
vehicle-geometry.js and boost-effects.js: cars and Nitro.
route-road.js: non-overlapping asphalt for forked routes.
public/game-core.js and the three language banks in public are readable runtime files.
Install the dependencies from package.json with npm, then run npm run build.
npm test checks full gameplay. Additional checks include test:ulti,
test:road-bounds, test:fairness, test:clear-roads, test:rivals, test:pacing,
test:crosswalk, test:acceleration, test:yielding, test:racing, test:reading,
test:routes, test:scene, test:presentation, test:overdrive, test:nitro-hold,
test:spectators and test:ui.
